newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia T-bills yield seen at mkt level at Wed sale.
newsitem.headline: Russia T-bills yield seen at mkt level at Wed sale.

text.p: Cheap roubles will spark increased demand at Wednesday's auctions of Russian GKO discount Treasury bills, reversing a recent lack of market liquidity and preserving yields at current levels, dealers said on Tuesday.
A rouble shortage on the interbank market last week prevented many banks from actively trading government securities. But this week the interbank market eased and T-bill trading became livelier.
ON WEDNESDAY
THE FINANCE MINISTRY SELLS:
*5.50 trln rbls in 119-day T-bills (series 21087)
*8.00 trln rbls in 364-day T-bills (series 21086)
THE FINANCE MINISTRY REPAYS:
*9.51 trln rbls in 227-day series 22065 T-bills
ON TUESDAY
*Average yield on taxable T-bills fell to 18.72 pct from 18.87 pct on Monday
*Average yield on taxable floating rate OFZ bonds rose to 32.18 pct from 31.93 pct
*Turnover rose to 3.00 trln rbls from 2.24 trln rbls
*Central bank did not intervene on the market
*Banks transferred 1.91 trln rbls for trading

Dealers forecast the average yield for the 119-day T-bill to be 17.92-18.29 percent. Series 22074 bills, maturing on December 10, 1997, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 94.69 on Tuesday, to yield 18.11 percent.

Dealers forecast the average yield for the 364-day T-bill to be 18.83-19.13 percent. Series 21085 bills, maturing on August 12, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 84.27 on Tuesday, to yield 19.03 percent.

"Monday and Tuesday showed that the situation on the rouble/dollar market is stable. Overnight credits are not expensive and that is why we are not likely to get a premium," CS First Boston dealer Sergei Koshelenko said.
Dealers estimated the maximum rise of the yield above market levels at between 0.10 and 0.15 percentage points.
"Roubles appeared on the market and that is why the demand at tomorrow's auctions will be enough," United City Bank dealer Stanislav Kuchinsky said.
